source_message.speaker: client
source_message.text:
Hi [FREELANCER_NAME_001],

After comparing the kerning studies together, I am definitely most attracted to Option 2 (Balanced Flow). It reads as one unified word but still retains the airiness and elegance we have been developing.

Before proceeding with the material treatments, I want to reconsider the terminal used by the Hero V, second V, and É accent.

We devoted substantial time to perfecting the Hero V before the rest of the alphabet had been created. At that point, the Hero V had to express far more of the identity by itself. With the complete wordmark now assembled, I no longer think it needs to be so expressive or decorative.

I’m seeking a feeling of precision, assurance, and quiet elevation. I’d like to test a terminal that appears more deliberate and architectural—a restrained, controlled upward release instead of a flourish.

I’m attaching two references that start to convey the quality I mean. I do not want either one reproduced exactly, but their cleaner transitions and more restrained elevation appeal to me.

The established structure and slope of both the Hero V and second V should remain unchanged. Instead, please create a few interpretations that preserve that geometry while applying a consistently refined terminal to the Hero V, second V, and É accent.

Thank you!

value_updates.terminal_style: Use the same deliberate, architectural, restrained, and controlled upward-release terminal as the Hero V and second V rather than an expressive or decorative flourish.

decisions.reason: The terminal study applies only to the Hero V, second V, and É accent; the established E and L letterform requirements remain unchanged.
The client preserves the second V's established structure and changes only its terminal, so its height relationship and restrained hierarchy remain valid unchanged.
The existing message-189 MODIFY already records the client's selection of Option 2 (Balanced Flow), and the accompanying verification records its unified reading.
Refining the shared terminal does not cancel or alter the requirement that the É accent and Hero V peaks share the same horizontal reference line.
The terminal redesign changes geometry but does not change which signature elements receive champagne gold.
Reconsidering the terminal before proceeding with material treatments is sequencing context and does not modify the selected Satin Reflection finish or its required character.
The source message contains no decision about review-file formats or delivery accessibility.
The terminal study preserves the established geometry and does not alter the shared-baseline relationship.
